land.text: the Yucatán peninsula, lost to the federalist rebels: Valladolid on 12 February 1840, Campeche on 6 June 1840

predecessors.note: Formal independence only on 16 March 1841; the Republic page treats the 1841-1848 span as the republic, with a first period of sovereignty from the 1840 rising.

land.text: Yucatán rejoins Mexico: 'August 17 of that year, Barbachano ordered the resumption of a confederation of Mexico'

successors.note: The infobox gives "Disestablished: July 14 1848" (the day Mexico sent 150,000 pesos).

land.text: the south-east held by the Maya after the Caste War; the Chan Santa Cruz page gives 1849 as the state's proclamation

successors.note: Infobox "Succeeded by" is garbled on the page; Chan Santa Cruz is read from its own infobox ("Preceded by: Republic of Yucatan").

capitals.name: Campeche
capitals.note: "On January 21, 1847, Santiago Méndez moved the Yucatán capital to Campeche." The page does not say the capital returned to Mérida before August 1848.

correction.text: Captain Santiago Imán took Valladolid on 12 February 1840 and 'proclaimed the independence of the Yucatecan territory'; Campeche still held by the centralists until 6 June 1840

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row. The page gives no extent for the first months of the rising; the Yucatán state is the researcher's reading, Campeche joins on 6 June 1840 (ledger). Quintana Roo (then the eastern part of the state of Yucatán) was added by the reviewer (am-08-x, 2026-10-19): the page says 'The area of the former republic includes the modern Mexican states of Yucatán, Campeche and Quintana Roo', and centralist-mexico loses all three in June 1840.

correction.text: the former republic 'covered the modern states of Yucatán, Campeche, and Quintana Roo'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area; the three states of the modern peninsula are the page's own statement of the republic's area. The Petén annexation 'was repeatedly postponed and shelved around 1856' and was never completed; Belize is not claimed. Between Santa Anna's convention of 5 December 1843 and the Mexican Congress's late-1845 revocation 'the Republic retained its sovereignty', so the shape is unchanged for 1844-1845.

correction.text: by spring 1848 Maya forces held most of the peninsula 'except the walled cities of Campeche and Mérida and the southwest coast'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Caste War page gives the Maya gains of spring 1848; the radii (Mérida 60 km, Campeche 80 km for the south-west coast) are the researcher's reading. The Maya-held interior is the contest zone (ledger) and later the Chan Santa Cruz state; the siege of Mérida was broken later, undated on the page.

region.text: Santiago Imán's rising from Valladolid: 'Captain Santiago Imán proclaimed the independence of the Yucatecan territory'

ledger.note: 12 February 1840: Captain Santiago Imán takes Valladolid and calls for federalism. 'on February 12, 1840 issued a report, which stated that federalism should be restored'; the independence of 'the Yucatecan territory' is proclaimed six days later. The Republic page's own independence date is 16 March 1841.

region.text: the walled city of Campeche, which 'surrendered to the Yucatecan Federalists after a military siege'

ledger.note: 6 June 1840: Campeche surrenders to the Yucatecan federalists. 'On June 6, 1840, the city of Campeche surrendered to the Yucatecan Federalists after a military siege.' Mexico then 'declared war on the Yucatán'.

16 March 1841: Yucatán declares itself independent. 'On March 16, 1841 at the first City Council meeting in Mérida' a crowd led by Miguel Barbachano Terrazo called for independence; the constitution was promulgated on 31 March and the Act of Independence adopted on 1 October 1841. Not a name change: the federalist state of 1840 becomes the Republic, colour continues.

region.text: Carmen Island and the Campeche coast, where the Mexican squadron formed and 'took the island without encountering armed resistance'

ledger.note: August 1842: Santa Anna sends the navy against Yucatán. 'In August 1842, a Mexican naval squadron formed off Carmen Island' and its soldiers took the island a few days later; 'after several failed attempts to take Campeche' the Mexicans went on towards Mérida. The page is silent on when Carmen was recovered.

5 December 1843: Santa Anna grants Yucatán autonomy. 'Santa Anna agreed to several conditions giving full autonomy to the Yucatán on December 5, 1843'; 'the Republic retained its sovereignty'. General Peña y Barragán had already agreed to withdraw his troops by sea on 24 April 1843.

1 January 1846: Yucatán declares independence a second time. 'In late 1845, the Mexican Congress revoked the Conventions of December 1843' and 'the Assembly of Yucatán declared its independence on January 1, 1846'. Not a name change: the schema has no declaration event, so the second period of sovereignty is marked here; colour continues.
21 January 1847: the capital moves to Campeche. 'On January 21, 1847, Santiago Méndez moved the Yucatán capital to Campeche.'

region.text: the peninsula outside the walled cities: 'Maya forces held most of the peninsula, except the walled cities of Campeche and Mérida and the southwest coast' (spring 1848)

ledger.note: 30 July 1847: the Caste War breaks out at Tepich. 'Cecilio Chi, the Maya leader of Tepich, with Jacinto Pat attacked Tepich on 30 July 1847.' The Maya rebels are the Chan Santa Cruz state's predecessors; the zone is the researcher's reading of the spring-1848 front.

region.text: the Maya-held interior at the Republic's end

ledger.note: August 1848: Yucatán rejoins Mexico while the war goes on. 'Yucatán was officially reunited with Mexico' on 17 August 1848; the south-east stays Maya, and from 1849-1850 it is the Chan Santa Cruz state (a separate dossier). The contest continues in the Mexican and Chan Santa Cruz dossiers.

region.text: Yucatán and Campeche, back in the Mexican confederation

ledger.note: 17 August 1848: Yucatán rejoins Mexico. 'August 17 of that year, Barbachano ordered the resumption of a confederation of Mexico'; Mexico had sent 150,000 pesos on 14 July 1848.

region.text: the Republic of Yucatán, ended by the Caste War and reunion with Mexico

ledger.note: 1848: the Republic of Yucatán ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: July 14 1848'; the text has Barbachano order the resumption of the confederation on 17 August 1848. Both pages put the end in the summer of 1848.

wars.name: Mexican campaign against Yucatán

zones.text: Campeche, Carmen Island and the road to Mérida

wars.outcome: Negotiated settlement: Campeche fell to the federalists on 6 June 1840; the Mexican squadron took Carmen Island in August 1842; General Peña y Barragán withdrew by sea on 24 April 1843; Santa Anna's conditions of 5 December 1843 gave Yucatán 'full autonomy'.
wars.note: The Mexican Congress revoked the conventions in late 1845; Yucatán declared independence again on 1 January 1846.

wars.name: Mexican–American War
wars.outcome: No territorial result for Yucatán: it declared neutrality; 'In October 1846, the US Navy took Ciudad del Carmen, and blockaded Yucatán'; a delegation under José Rovira argued in Washington that neutrality should protect it.
wars.note: Only the Yucatán side is recorded here. In 1848 a second delegation under Justo Sierra O'Reilly offered to annex the peninsula to the United States; the Caste War page says Congress debated it with 'no will to fight'.

wars.name: Caste War of Yucatán
wars.outcome: Yucatán was nearly lost: by spring 1848 the Maya held most of the peninsula; the republic rejoined Mexico on 17 August 1848; the south-east became the Chan Santa Cruz state, which Mexico occupied in 1901.
wars.note: Years follow the Chan Santa Cruz page (state to 1901); the page also has the war 'officially declared over for the final time in September 1915'. This dossier's part ends in August 1848.

certainty.note: The peninsula's coast is sharp; the south-eastern frontier with the Maya, the border with Belize and the Petén line are approximate and no treaty line is dated on the pages opened.

notes:
Cliopatria has no Republic of Yucatán row. Counterparts: centralist-mexico (1840 gain, 1842-43 contest; its own dossier mirrors them) and federated-republic-of-mexico (1848 merge); chan-santa-cruz is written in this batch.
Start: the infobox gives independence on 16 March 1841; the dossier starts in February 1840 with Imán's rising so that the loss recorded in centralist-mexico (June 1840) has a matching gain. The 1841 and 1846 declarations are marked as `rename` events only because the schema has no declaration event.
End: infobox 14 July 1848 against 17 August 1848 in the text; August is used.
Page limits: the Republic page gives no area and no extent for 1840; the 1848 Maya-held zone and the radii around Mérida and Campeche are the researcher's reading of 'most of the peninsula, except the walled cities of Campeche and Mérida and the southwest coast'. Carmen Island (taken by Mexico in August 1842, held by the US Navy in October 1846) has no recovery date on the page. Rulers are not listed: the infobox gives only Santiago Méndez (first, 1840-1841) and Miguel Barbachano (last, 1847-1848; he took office in April 1848).
